subject: PrivPool headroom: warmup cadence, egress throttling & operational runbook
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <sam@brightlane.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivPool headroom: warmup cadence, egress throttling & operational runbook

Team / Sam —

We need a short runbook and concrete numbers for Brightlane's private GPU pool for the initial launch next month. Goals: sustain 1.5M tokens/min aggregate with 95th-pct latency < 250ms on 16k-context chat workloads, and a warmup cadence that avoids cold-start spikes during peak business hours (US PST).

Asks:
- Karthik: can you provide expected steady-state host counts and a 3-point headroom plan (conservative, target, aggressive) with assumptions for batching and KV-cache hit rates?
- Jonas: network/egress constraints — minimum cross-connect throughput and a per-instance NIC oversubscription ratio we should design to. Also any suggested egress throttles to prevent noisy tenant storms.
- Sam: Brightlane ops — confirm whether you can provision BGP route priorities and a burstable 10Gbps egress pool for the first 4 weeks.

I attached a warmup_profile_v1.xlsx that outlines current warm-pool heuristics (idle timeout, pre-warm batch size, ramp durations). Please reply with numbers by EOD Monday so we can finalize the runbook and playbook to hand off to Customer Ops.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
attachments: warmup_profile_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <sam@brightlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 12:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivPool headroom: warmup cadence, egress throttling & operational runbook

Thanks for the context, Olga. High-level numbers (quick summary) — detailed assumptions and CSV attached (privpool_throughput_model.csv).

Assumptions: 16k chat average request = 420 tokens generated per request; average prompt tokens 80; KV-cache hit 48% (with prefix caching warmed from warm-pool); batching size avg = 6 requests; GPU type = a40-v2 equivalent.

Steady-state host counts (instances serving concurrently):
- Conservative: 12 hosts — expected throughput ~0.9M tokens/min (safe for bursty tail)
- Target: 20 hosts — ~1.6M tokens/min (meets 1.5M target with 10% slack)
- Aggressive: 28 hosts — ~2.2M tokens/min (for heavy peak days)
Warmup cadence recommendation (to keep cold starts < 3% of requests):
- Pre-warm 25% of target pool 15 minutes before local business window (08:30 PST).
- Additional incremental warm-up of 25% at T+5 and final 50% T+10; keep pre-warm idle TTL = 22 minutes.
Headroom policy: maintain target plan (20 hosts) with automatic +20% burst (up to 24) using predictive autoscale and fallback to aggressive plan if sustained >85% CPU for 6m.
I've attached throughput model with per-host qps and token math. Happy to walk through numbers Monday.
-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
attachments: privpool_throughput_model.csv (text/csv, 92KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <sam@brightlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivPool headroom: warmup cadence, egress throttling & operational runbook

Looping in my notes on networking and guardrails. Quoting Karthik for context: "Target: 20 hosts — ~1.6M tokens/min".

Network constraints & recommendations:
- Cross-connect minimum: provision 40Gbps dedicated with 2x 40Gbps LAG where available. We want headroom for egress offload and a buffer for cross-tenant bursts.
- NIC oversubscription: do not oversubscribe >1.8x for inference traffic; practice 1.3x when tenants are noisy.
- Egress shaping: implement token-bucket policing per-tenant at the ToR (suggested default = 6Gbps per-tenant, configurable). For Brightlane initial rollout, we should carve a shared burst pool of 10Gbps that is rate-limited by priority rules.
- Burst isolation: prefer DSCP marking for high-priority inference flows and place them in a higher queue. If BGP route priority is available, use it to prefer warm-pool replication traffic over bulk backups during business hours.
Failure modes to design for:
- Link saturation -> fall back to local batching (reduce pre-warm batch size from 6 -> 3) and increase KV-cache TTL to avoid regen.
- Noisy tenant -> automated tenant-level throttle + circuit-breaker at 75% NIC utilization.
I will draft an egress_policy_draft.md with the shaping rules and sample tc/iptables snippets.
-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Staff Network Engineer

From: Samir Patel <sam@brightlane.com>

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivPool headroom: warmup cadence, egress throttling & operational runbook

Thanks — Brightlane can provision the networking primitives requested. Quick confirmations: 
- We can stand up a 2x40Gbps LAG and reserve a 10Gbps burst pool for 30 days. BGP route priority changes are allowed during the rollout windows (we will need a short change window).
- Ops will apply tenant token-bucket by default. We require the final shaping rules (Jonas) to implement; please send the draft.
Request: can Redwood provide a small sidecar script that will signal us back when pre-warm is complete per rack/host? That would be helpful to coordinate route preference flips and telemetry gating.

If you can ship the runbook and the shaping draft by EOD today, we’ll schedule the change for Friday 21 Aug 02:00-04:00 PST.

-Samir
Samir Patel
SRE Lead, Brightlane

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivPool headroom: warmup cadence, egress throttling & operational runbook

Great — outlined decisions and next steps below (finalizing runbook). Quoting salient commitments: Brightlane -> 2x40Gbps LAG + 10Gbps burst pool for 30d; Redwood -> pre-warm cadence automation + small sidecar signal; Jonas -> egress shaping draft; Karthik -> autoscale thresholds and host counts (CSV delivered).

Final runbook bullets (to be published to Drive link):
1) Launch target: 20 hosts (1.6M tokens/min). Autoscale policy: +20% burst up to 24; fallback to +40% (28) on sustained 6m >85% GPU util.
2) Warmup: 25% pre-warm 15m prior, +25% at T+5, +50% at T+10. Sidecar will emit /ready events; Brightlane will hold route priority flip until 90% of expected sidecars report ready per-rack.
3) Network: 2x40Gbps LAG; NIC oversubscription <=1.8x; tenant policing token-bucket default 6Gbps; shared 10Gbps burst pool. DSCP marking for inference traffic.
4) Operational play: if NIC utilization >75% trigger tenant circuit-breaker; reduce batch size (6 -> 3) and increase cache TTL to 60m.
5) Rollout window: Friday 21 Aug 02:00-04:00 PST (pending change ticket).

I'll publish the runbook to the Drive link and attach the shaping draft and throughput CSV. Will follow up with an ops checklist for the Friday window. Thanks everyone for quick turn.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
